The functions are pure, with no outside calls, so they are easy to check.

terms.meaning: The range of times and probabilities that the scaling maps onto the picture.

sections.name: WpPoint, Box
sections.title: Point and box shapes
sections.what: Defines the shape of a point (a time and a win probability) and of the drawing box (width, height and padding).
sections.why: Gives every helper the same inputs.

sections.name: scale, r
sections.title: Scaling helper
sections.what: Builds functions that turn times and probabilities into positions on the picture, keeping probabilities between zero and one.
sections.why: Lets a chart fit any range of times and probabilities.
sections.watch_out: A single time value makes the span one, so every point lands on the left edge.

sections.name: linePath, Swing
sections.title: Line path and swing shape
sections.what: Turns a list of points into drawing text for a line, and defines the shape of a swing. Returns empty text for an empty list.
sections.why: Gives the chart a line to draw.
sections.watch_out: The main line and the estimate must share the same domain, or they will not line up.

sections.name: swings
sections.title: Finding swings
sections.what: Finds each step where the win probability moved by at least the threshold, and returns the list largest first.
sections.why: Marks the moments that changed the match.
sections.watch_out: The sort changes the order, so code that relies on position must not use this list directly.

sections.name: windowSwing
sections.title: Window change
sections.what: Returns the net change in win probability between the first and last point of a window, or zero for fewer than two points.
sections.why: Summarises how much a stretch of the match moved overall.
sections.watch_out: It measures net change, not the largest move, so a swing up and back down shows as zero.

summary: Pure helper functions that turn win-probability points into positions, line drawings and swing lists for the chart.
purpose: Holds the maths behind the Swing Seismograph chart so it can be tested separately.
why: Keeping the maths out of the component makes it easy to test and reuse.
how: Defines the point and box shapes, builds scaling functions, turns points into an SVG line path, finds steps above a threshold, and measures the net change of a window.
inputs: Lists of time and win-probability points, box dimensions, and a threshold for swings.
outputs: Scaling functions, path text for drawing, a sorted list of swings, and a net change value.
risks: Scaling with a single time value puts every point at the left edge. Forgetting to pass a shared domain makes two lines scale differently. A swing up and back down shows as zero in the net change.
debug: If a line is off-screen, check the domain and box sizes. If swings look wrong, check the threshold. If the window change looks zero, check whether the start and end values match.
